defect_observations.observation: 'The other order similarly gives G(z-x)' stands in for the inner-integral computation behind the second displayed cumulative identity; counted partial (see component gap). A one-line display int 1{x+y<=z} dnu(y) = nu((-inf,z-x]) = G(z-x), or an explicit appeal to the first identity for (nu,mu) plus the proved commutativity, would close it.

'The same derivative argument proves, for any r>0, c>0, that x^r e^{-cx/2} is bounded' extends the written c=1 sign argument (lines 238-242) to general c; the normal second-moment proof uses the c=1/2 instance at lines 456-458. Not counted partial (not a listed marker; the parameter-uniform sign computation is identified), but a reading that treats 'the same argument' as 'similarly' would make C014 partial.
'The change y=zu, z>0, similarly gives' qualifies an explicitly named affine substitution whose transformed integral is displayed (309-316); counted as written.
'Interchanging f,g proves the same for {g>f}': the written argument uses only symmetric hypotheses, so this is an instantiation; counted as written.
'The case b=0 is the same argument with the variables interchanged': instantiation of the written a=0 case for the pair (Y,X); counted as written.

'Fixing y instead proves the other marginal identity': instantiation of the written fixed-x argument for the pair (Y,X); counted as written. Similar named interchanges at finite annex 158 and 168-169 (C011) and Stirling annex 196 (C004, p_n(-k)=p_n(k)) were also counted as written.
